decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a heavily invested, publicly announced product with a US release still pending, so management would attribute any early weak sales to the rollout timing and stay committed.
Small volume chambers are core dosimetry products that fit the firm's precision-measurement identity and need little upkeep, so there is no reason to drop it this early.
Although it overlaps with Product B, this newly launched chamber has sunk development and certification costs, and a recent launch decision would need justifying, so the firm keeps it.
The standard clinical chamber line has several models, is central to the firm's established calibration and dosimetry business, and stays.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantoms and QA workflows, so it is strategically aligned and retained.
Thimble chambers are staple reference instruments with steady demand and accredited calibration support, so the firm keeps it.
